name: mc_restore
title: Restore snapshot or undo a journalled call
description:
Undoes earlier changes in one of two ways: restores a snapshot's whole region, or undoes one journalled tool call (mc_build, mc_repair or mc_restore) cell by cell.

WHEN TO USE: a build or repair went wrong; a user asks to undo, revert or roll back a change. Prefer `journal` when other work may have happened in the area since: safe mode restores only cells that still hold what that call wrote and reports the rest as conflicts, so later builds and hand edits survive. Use `id` (a snapshot) to reset a whole region to one moment, for example while iterating on an experiment. Find journal ids in the build response or with mc_snapshot {action:"journal-list", touches:{from,to}}.

WHEN NOT TO USE: to look at a region's contents (use mc_inspect or mc_diff). To list snapshots (mc_snapshot action:"list") or journal entries (action:"journal-list").

PARAMETERS: exactly one of `id` (snapshot id) or `journal` (journal id). Journal options: `mode` "safe" (default) or "force" (also overwrites cells changed since and reports how many); `dryRun:true` reports what would happen without writing; `allowBlockEntityReplacement:true` also replaces cells that now hold signs, chests or other block entities (skipped by default); `samples` limits listed conflicts (default 20). There are no coordinates: the snapshot or journal entry fixes the world and cells.

SIDE EFFECTS: a snapshot restore overwrites its whole region with the captured states. A journal undo writes only the original states of that call's changed cells, without physics or a connection pass (neighbour shapes the call changed are journalled too). Both are journalled themselves, so an undo can be undone. Snapshots and journals store block states only: sign text, inventories and entities are not restored. Unknown or evicted ids are rejected without changes; journal entries expire (journal.max-age-days) and are evicted oldest first.

id.description: Snapshot id, e.g. "snap-20260913-220102-a3f9", as returned by mc_snapshot or mc_build with snapshot:true. Not with `journal`.

journal.description: Journal id, e.g. "jrn-20261010-120239-aa42", from a build/repair/restore response or mc_snapshot journal-list. Undoes only that call.

mode.description: Journal undo only. safe: restore cells still holding what the call wrote; force: restore every cell, overwriting later changes.

dryRun.description: Journal undo only. Report restorable cells and conflicts without writing.

allowBlockEntityReplacement.description: Journal undo only. Also replace cells that now hold a block entity (sign text, inventory), which is lost.

samples.description: Journal undo only. Maximum conflict samples listed.
